summary: Fail closed for meal-calendar writes that acknowledge HTTP success without read-back persistence.
reason: A disposable marker probe sent the typed candidate new-event operation to /data/meal-planning-calendar/update and received HTTP 200, but a fresh user-data read omitted the event. The cleanup delete-event operation also returned HTTP 200 and the marker remained absent. Until a complete create/update/delete round-trip is verified, meal add and delete must not perform live mutations or report success; dry-run previews remain available.
validated_outcome: Non-dry-run meal add/delete now return explicit unsupported read-after-write-verification errors before any request. Focused tests cover both fail-closed paths and preserve JSON dry-run previews for both commands. The disposable marker event was absent on fresh read-back after the acknowledged create and after cleanup; no production meal data was changed.
